items.question: Your CFO asks why the company should move from on-premises to AWS. What do you say?
items.answer: Cloud shifts capital expenditure on hardware to operational expenditure you scale with demand. You provision capacity in minutes across global Regions instead of waiting for procurement cycles. AWS operates physical security, power, and hardware refresh. You retain responsibility for architecture, security configuration, and cost governance — cloud is not automatic savings without tagging, rightsizing, and architecture discipline.
followUps: How do Availability Zones change your disaster recovery story?
items.sixtySeconds: Opex and elasticity. Global Regions. AWS runs data centers; you run architecture and security config. Savings need governance — tags, right-sizing, egress awareness.

items.question: A security auditor blames AWS for a public S3 data leak. How do you respond?
items.answer: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS secures the physical infrastructure and S3 service foundation. Bucket policies, Block Public Access settings, encryption choices, and IAM permissions are customer responsibilities. The fix is enabling account-level Block Public Access, auditing bucket policies with S3 Storage Lens or IAM Access Analyzer, and enforcing least-privilege roles — not expecting AWS to default-deny public access on your behalf.
followUps: How does responsibility shift between EC2 and Lambda?
What does AWS Config add to this picture?
items.sixtySeconds: AWS secures the cloud; you secure in the cloud. Public S3 is customer misconfiguration. Enable Block Public Access, audit policies, least-privilege IAM.

items.question: Your app can read S3 objects but CloudTrail shows no object access. Why?
items.answer: Default CloudTrail captures management events (control plane) like CreateBucket and PutBucketPolicy. S3 GetObject and PutObject are data plane operations. To audit object access, enable CloudTrail data events for the bucket or S3 server access logging. This plane distinction is fundamental — management audit and data audit use different mechanisms.
followUps: How would you restrict a role to data plane only?
What is the difference between CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs?
items.sixtySeconds: CloudTrail default = control plane. Object GET/PUT needs data events or S3 access logs. Split planes in IAM and observability.

items.question: Design a simple three-tier web API on AWS — name services by category.
items.answer: DNS via Route 53, optional CDN via CloudFront. Application Load Balancer in public subnets routes HTTPS to compute — ECS Fargate or EC2 depending on operational preference. RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets for relational state. S3 for user uploads. SQS for async order processing with Lambda consumers. IAM roles per tier. VPC with public/private subnets and NAT for outbound-only private instances.
followUps: When would DynamoDB replace RDS here?
Why put RDS in a private subnet?
items.sixtySeconds: Route 53, CloudFront, ALB, ECS/EC2, RDS, S3, SQS, Lambda, IAM, VPC. Category first, then flagship service.

items.question: Monthly AWS bill jumped 40% with no traffic increase. Where do you look first?
items.answer: Cost Explorer grouped by service and tag — NAT Gateway, data transfer out, idle EC2/RDS, and unattached Elastic IPs are frequent culprits. Check for untagged dev resources left running. Review inter-AZ transfer if microservices chatter across zones. Enable Cost Anomaly Detection and Budgets alarms proactively. Verify no accidental cross-Region replication or public S3 egress spike.
followUps: How do Savings Plans interact with autoscaling?
What tags do you require at resource creation?
items.sixtySeconds: Cost Explorer by service and tag. Check NAT, egress, idle compute, Elastic IPs. Tags and Budgets prevent repeat surprises.

items.question: CI deploy fails with LimitExceeded on EC2. What happened and how do you fix it?
items.answer: You hit a service quota — default On-Demand EC2 instance limits per Region are low. The deploy pipeline tried to launch more instances than the quota allows. Request a quota increase via Service Quotas console or API before launch milestones. Also check if orphaned instances from failed deploys consume the quota — terminate stale resources and use Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to prevent drift.
followUps: How do SCPs interact with service quotas?
What is the difference between soft and hard quotas?
items.sixtySeconds: Service quota hit — not IAM. Request increase via Service Quotas API. Clean orphaned instances. Plan quotas before prod launch.

items.question: Explain IaaS versus PaaS using AWS examples relevant to a Node.js team.
items.answer: IaaS: EC2 runs your Node process — you patch the OS, manage the process supervisor, and configure Security Groups. PaaS-style: Lambda runs your handler — AWS manages the runtime container, you upload code and set memory/timeout. Elastic Beanstalk is a middle ground — you deploy a Node app; AWS manages capacity and load balancer wiring. Pick based on operational burden versus control.
followUps: When is Fargate a better fit than Lambda?
How does cold start affect the choice?
items.sixtySeconds: EC2 = IaaS, you own OS. Lambda = function PaaS, AWS owns runtime. Beanstalk = opinionated deploy. Match ops burden to team skill.
